subject.title: [Feature]: Feature Request: Batch Tool Calls + Context Block Management + Plan Enforcement

question: Should OpenClaw pursue any of these native core surfaces now: file/search batching, AI-callable context blocks, or runner-enforced submitted plans?
rationale: The request changes core tool schemas, context/session persistence semantics, config surface, and enforcement policy, while repository vision only partially aligns and warns against heavy orchestration or optional capability that can live through plugin/API seams.

options.title: Split for design review
options.body: Keep this umbrella open and ask maintainers to sponsor narrower design tracks for any surface they want to pursue.

options.title: Route pieces to plugins or existing APIs
options.body: Defer core changes unless a missing plugin/API seam is proven, using Parallel Search, context-engine hooks, and plugin surfaces where adequate.

options.title: Decline native core scope
options.body: Close the direction if maintainers decide native batching, AI-controlled context blocks, and strict plan enforcement are not planned for core.

recommendation.title: Split for design review
recommendation.body: Keep this umbrella open and ask maintainers to sponsor narrower design tracks for any surface they want to pursue.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest adjacent history across update_plan, strict-agentic behavior, current tool-schema code, and the prior product-review comments on this issue.
